name: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
venue: NeurIPS 2024 (38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, poster; OpenReview id tBRNC6YemY, accepted 25 Sept 2024). Originally arXiv:2305.15334 (cs.CL), submitted 24 May 2023.
authors_affiliation: Shishir G. Patil (UC Berkeley), Tianjun Zhang (UC Berkeley) [equal contribution], Xin Wang (Microsoft Research), Joseph E. Gonzalez (UC Berkeley). Project from the UC Berkeley Sky Computing Lab / RISELab.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla (continuously maintained; now also hosts the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard / BFCL, the Gorilla API Zoo, OpenFunctions, GoEx, and RAFT). Leaderboard at https://gorilla.cs.berkeley.edu/leaderboard.html
task_domain: tool-use (LLM tool/API calling): given a natural-language request, select and write the correct fully-qualified ML API call from a massive, overlapping, and changing set of APIs. Also touches code (single-line API-call program synthesis).
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, non-interactive single-turn API-call generation. The model receives a natural-language user intent and must emit one correct, fully-qualified API call (e.g. torch.hub.load(...)) drawn from a large corpus of ML APIs scraped from TorchHub, TensorFlow Hub, and HuggingFace. Supervision is self-instruct: GPT-4 synthesizes ~10 instruction-API pairs per API from 18 hand-written seed examples; a LLaMA-7B base model is finetuned on these (instruction -> reference API) pairs. Two inference modes are supported: zero-shot (no retriever) and retrieval-augmented (a retriever appends the most relevant API documentation to the prompt). The key novelty is Retriever-Aware Training (RAT): during finetuning the retrieved (oracle) API document is appended to the prompt so the model learns to ground its answer in provided documentation, enabling test-time adaptation to changed/updated API docs. No environment execution or multi-step planning is part of the evaluated task (an execution engine exists but is out of scope).
what_is_retrieved: tools / docs: API documentation (model cards converted to structured JSON with fields domain, framework, functionality, api_name, api_call, api_arguments, environment_requirements, example_code, performance, description) for candidate ML APIs from TorchHub / TensorFlow Hub / HuggingFace.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed API documentation database (APIBench, 1,645 ML API model cards). Retrieval targets this static doc store; the method explicitly stresses that the store can be UPDATED at test time (version/document changes) but is not an agent-written growing episodic memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-1 ranking objective: the retriever fetches the single most relevant API document (top-1) and appends it to the prompt. Not a complete-minimal-set or precision-driven variable-size recommendation; a single API call is generated and evaluated.
retrieval_unit: tool-API document: one API's documentation (a model card rendered as a JSON object) is treated as a single retrievable document; each API is indexed as a separate document.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-built from scraped public model hubs: 95 TorchHub APIs, 696 TensorFlow Hub APIs (after filtering low-information cards), and 925 HuggingFace APIs (top-20 most-downloaded per domain), totaling 1,645 API documents. The store is designed to be editable/updatable at test time (documentation change experiments) but does not grow via agent self-writing.
index_structure_topology: Flat document index: each API documentation entry is one independent document. BM25 uses a term index over these documents; GPT-Index/GPT retriever indexes each API as an individual document. No dependency graph or hierarchical/category topology is used for retrieval (domain metadata exists in the cards but retrieval is flat per-document). [uncertain] whether any clustering is applied internally.
retriever_type: hybrid set of off-the-shelf retrievers evaluated: BM25 (sparse term-based), GPT-Index (dense retrieval using OpenAI text-davinci-003 embeddings), plus an Oracle retriever (ground-truth document, upper bound). The retriever is external/frozen; Gorilla itself is the generator, not a learned retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: none (off-the-shelf retrievers: BM25, GPT-Index/text-davinci-003, Oracle are not trained). The learning happens in the GENERATOR via Retriever-Aware Training: the LLaMA-7B model is finetuned with the (oracle) retrieved document appended, i.e. supervised next-token loss conditioned on retrieved documentation, teaching the model to parse and ground on retrieved docs. There is no contrastive or RL training of the retriever component.
query_construction: Raw natural-language user instruction is used as the query to the retriever; the top-1 retrieved API documentation is concatenated to the user prompt with the fixed string 'Use this API documentation for reference:' before being fed to Gorilla. No query decomposition, expansion, or intent extraction.
query_granularity: task-level: a single retrieval is performed once per user request (t=0) using the raw instruction; one API call is produced.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot: a single retrieval call per query (in retrieval mode). Zero-shot mode performs no retrieval at all. No iterative or uncertainty-triggered retrieval.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule / mode switch: retrieval is either always-on (retrieval mode, one retrieval per query) or always-off (zero-shot mode). There is no learned router, confidence signal, or agent-initiated trigger deciding when to retrieve; the mode is set by the user/system configuration.
reranking: None. The top-1 document from BM25 / GPT-Index is used directly; no cross-encoder, RRF, or hierarchy-aware reranking stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: None. The retrieved API documentation is appended verbatim to the prompt (prefixed by 'Use this API documentation for reference:'); no decompose-recompose, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression is applied.
tool_document_engineering: Tool/API descriptions are engineered into a uniform structured JSON schema before indexing: each scraped model card is converted into fields {domain, framework, functionality, api_name, api_call, api_arguments, environment_requirements, example_code, performance, description}, chosen to generalize beyond ML APIs to RESTful APIs. Low-information cards are filtered out. This is curated/normalized documentation rather than raw docstrings, but no synthetic-query augmentation or weighted-field tool embeddings are used for the index itself (self-instruct queries are used to train the generator, not to expand the index).
index_content_separation: No explicit lightweight-index-vs-heavy-content separation / progressive disclosure: the same per-API documentation object is both indexed and loaded into the prompt on retrieval. [uncertain]
dynamic_index_and_protocol: The API documentation database is designed to be UPDATED at test time (the paper demonstrates adapting to changed API docs, e.g. backbone upgrades ResNet-50 -> ResNet-101 and registry moves pytorch/vision -> NVIDIA/DeepLearningExamples:torchhub), so it supports manual/user updates of documents. Integration protocol in the paper is ML model-hub API calls (TorchHub/TensorFlow Hub/HuggingFace) with structured fields extensible to RESTful APIs; no automatic CRUD live-sync or MCP. (The broader follow-on Gorilla ecosystem adds the community API Zoo, OpenFunctions function-calling, and GoEx execution, but those are outside this paper.)
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A: the paper considers single, independent API calls (one API call per query) and explicitly does not model inter-tool dependencies, prerequisites, or chaining. It does model intra-call CONSTRAINTS (e.g. parameter size, minimum accuracy) that the chosen API must satisfy.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation + retriever-aware training signal: at inference the retrieved API doc is concatenated to the user prompt to ground generation; during training the same retrieved (oracle) doc is appended so the model learns to read and use retrieved documentation (Retriever-Aware Training). The output is a single API call to be invoked.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-generate (one-shot, no planning loop): in retrieval mode the retriever fetches the top-1 API document, which is appended to the prompt, then Gorilla generates the API call in a single forward pass. There is no MCTS/tree search, no per-step interleaving, and no multi-step plan; the task is single-call API selection.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer: one retrieval and one generation per user query; retrieval is not interleaved with multi-step reasoning, CoT steps, or multiple tool calls.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not framed as case-based reasoning). The closest analogue: the retrieved API document is used as grounding context that the retriever-aware-finetuned model conditions on to produce a correctly-instantiated API call (verbatim documentation injection + learned grounding), not case adaptation/revision.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw structured API documentation (the JSON model card text) injected into the prompt; the surface form is the documentation string, not a distilled strategy, workflow, or latent token.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw documentation / single reference item: the retrieved unit is the concrete API's documentation (a single candidate tool's spec), not a distilled strategy, guideline, reusable workflow, or procedural skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retriever-aware training (RAT): by finetuning with the retrieved document appended (and demonstrating that a non-optimal retriever can sometimes hurt), the model learns to ground on documentation and substantially reduce hallucination; AST sub-tree matching is used to detect/define hallucinations (an API call not matching any subtree in the database). The paper explicitly notes retrieval is not always beneficial (BM25/GPT-Index can mislead vs zero-shot), so robustness comes from finetuning-with-retrieval and from the zero-shot fallback rather than a relevance evaluator or self-reflection.
memory_type: none: no episodic/skill/workflow/graph/latent memory. The retrievable store is a static (editable) external API documentation database, not an agent-written memory.
write_back: false: the system does not write new experiences/cases/skills into a memory during deployment. (The API documentation store can be manually updated by users/maintainers, but the model does not self-write.)
online_growth: false: the API documentation index is frozen after offline construction; it can be manually edited/updated to reflect doc changes (the central test-time-adaptation feature) but it does not autonomously grow from the agent's own outputs at test time.
write_back_trigger: never: there is no automatic memory write-back. The only updates to the store are external/manual (human or maintainer editing API documents to reflect version/registry changes), demonstrated as the test-time documentation-change capability, not triggered by model success/failure or reflection.
failure_experience_usage: N/A / none: no experiences (success or failure) are stored or retrieved. Hallucinations and errors are measured and reduced via finetuning and AST matching, but failed outputs are not persisted as negative cases for retrieval.
memory_evolution_update: N/A: no stored experience entries to mutate. The external documentation store is updated only by manual/external editing (overwrite documents to new versions); there is no append/dedup/refine of model-written memory.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No: retrieval/document selection uses fixed off-the-shelf top-1 retrievers (BM25 / GPT-Index) or the Oracle; it is not an RL- or value-learned selection policy. The learned component is the document-grounded GENERATOR (retriever-aware finetuning), not the retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No: single-model setup with a private/shared static API store; no cross-agent or cross-framework experience sharing. (Gorilla can be plugged into agent frameworks like LangChain, but the paper does not study shared memory across agents.)
benchmarks: APIBench (introduced by this paper): 1,645 ML APIs across three model hubs - TorchHub (95 APIs, 6 domains), TensorFlow Hub (696 APIs, 57 domains), HuggingFace (925 APIs, 37 domains), each with ~10 self-instruct instruction-API pairs (held-out train/test split). Also a constraint-aware subset of TorchHub (the 65.26% of TorchHub entries with accuracy defined in their model card).
benchmark_family: tool (tool/API-use benchmark): APIBench is an ML-API tool-calling benchmark, predecessor in the same lineage that later grew into the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL). Functional correctness verified via AST sub-tree matching (verifiable answers).
baselines: Zero-shot SOTA LLMs: GPT-4 (gpt-4-0314), GPT-3.5-turbo (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301), Claude (claude-v1), and LLaMA-7B (base). Each is also evaluated under the same BM25, GPT-Index, and Oracle retrievers for fair comparison against Gorilla.
key_metrics: Overall AST functional-correctness accuracy (%, higher better); hallucination rate (%, lower better, defined via AST: an API call not a subtree of any DB API = imagined tool); error rate (%, wrong-but-real API). Constraint-aware setting additionally reports accuracy-constraint satisfaction. No latency/cost metrics in this paper (added later to BFCL).
headline_result: Lightly finetuned Gorilla (LLaMA-7B-based) in the zero-shot setting beats GPT-4 by 20.43% and GPT-3.5 by 10.75% in overall AST accuracy on APIBench, and outperforms LLaMA by ~83%, while substantially reducing hallucination. Per-hub zero-shot overall accuracy: TorchHub 59.13%, HuggingFace 71.68%, TensorFlow Hub 83.79%. Retriever-aware training with an oracle retriever pushes HuggingFace to 91.26% and TensorFlow Hub to 94.16% (Table 2).
ablations: (1) Finetuning vs retrieval: zero-shot finetuned Gorilla > adding off-the-shelf retrievers at test time; a non-optimal retriever (BM25/GPT-Index) at eval time can HURT, dropping accuracy by 21.50% on TorchHub and 47.57% on HuggingFace vs zero-shot. (2) Retriever-Aware Training (RAT): finetuning WITH the (oracle) retriever incorporated improves over finetuning without it by 12.37% on TorchHub and 23.46% on HuggingFace; but at eval time current retrievers still trail the ground-truth oracle (GPT-Index -29.20%, BM25 -52.27% accuracy gap). (3) Retriever quality sweep (zero-shot / BM25 / GPT-Index / Oracle) in Table 2 quantifies the accuracy-vs-hallucination tradeoff and the oracle upper bound. (4) Constraint-aware API invocation (Table 3): Gorilla matches the best model (GPT-3.5) with retrievers and has highest zero-shot accuracy under accuracy constraints. (5) RLHF/hallucination observation: GPT-3.5 hallucinates less than GPT-4 across all retriever settings.
evaluation_decoupling: Partial: results are reported as end-to-end overall AST accuracy decomposed into hallucination rate and error rate (an intrinsic-style breakdown of failure modes), and separately swept across retriever types (zero-shot/BM25/GPT-Index/oracle). However, standalone retriever metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) are NOT reported; the oracle retriever serves as the upper-bound proxy instead.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome: correctness of the single generated API call (overall accuracy), with a process-relevant decomposition into hallucination vs error and a constraint-satisfaction metric. No step-wise reasoning-faithfulness or trajectory-quality metrics (single-call task).
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency angle is model-size, not retrieval-call count: a small finetuned LLaMA-7B beats much larger GPT-4 zero-shot, and avoids costly retraining by adapting to updated docs via retrieval at test time. Training cost reported: 5 epochs, lr 2e-5 cosine decay, batch size 64, max seq length 2048, on 8xA100 (40GB). No explicit latency/API-cost/token-savings numbers in this paper (cost and latency metrics were added later to BFCL, 04/2024).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed top-1 selection: exactly one API document is retrieved and appended per query in retrieval mode; max sequence length 2048 tokens caps the prompt budget. Selection count is fixed (k=1), not adaptive or reranked-then-truncated.
benchmark_construction_and_size: APIBench size: 1,645 ML APIs (TorchHub 95, TensorFlow Hub 696, HuggingFace 925) with ~10 self-instruct instruction-API pairs each (~16,450 instruction-API datapoints). Construction: scrape public model-hub model cards -> filter low-information cards -> convert to structured JSON -> GPT-4 self-instruct generation from 18 hand-written seeds (3 hubs x 6 examples). Answer verifiability: AST sub-tree matching against the reference API (checks specific arguments, ignores optional/default args), which also defines hallucination. Difficulty signal: best zero-shot SOTA (GPT-4/GPT-3.5) reach only ~40% overall on TorchHub/TensorFlow Hub; oracle-retriever upper bounds reach ~67-94%.
builds_on: Self-Instruct (Wang et al. 2022) for synthetic instruction generation; LLaMA-7B (Touvron et al. 2023) as the finetuned base; instruction-tuned chat models Alpaca/Vicuna lineage; retrieval-augmented LM ideas (WebGPT, internet-augmented LMs); tool-use LLMs (Toolformer). Distinct claim: first to finetune a base model by supplementing it with information retrieval (retriever-aware training).
contrasts_with: Prompting-only tool-use methods that inject a small, well-documented API set into the context (Toolformer, HuggingGPT, TaskMatrix.AI) which cannot scale to millions of overlapping/changing APIs; and zero-shot prompting of GPT-4/GPT-3.5/Claude, which hallucinate API calls. Gorilla instead finetunes a small model with retrieval awareness over a large, updatable API documentation corpus.
lineage: Group E (tool-use): retrieval-augmented tool/API calling. A foundational static-corpus tool-retrieval-grounded method (retriever-aware finetuning over large API documentation) that selects/writes a single correct API call; predecessor of the Gorilla ecosystem (OpenFunctions, Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard / BFCL, API Zoo) and a reference point for later large-scale tool-retrieval work (e.g. ToolLLM/ToolBench, ToolRet).
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes (top-1 API document retrieval), Reuse: partial (retrieved doc used as grounding context, not a prior solved case), Revise: no, Retain: no]. Not a case-based-reasoning method; it retrieves documentation, not prior problem-solution cases.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False: the paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is retrieval-augmented finetuning for tool calling, not CBR.
